title: Phase Transition from Random Features to Fully Trainable Networks
abstract: arXiv:2610.31663v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Constructing accurate and computationally tractable approximation spaces is a fundamental task in scientific computing. Partially trainable neural networks bridge fixed random features and fully adaptive representations. This paper quantifies a phase transition pattern in approximation bounds and observes analogous behavior in training errors: a rapid but smooth initial improvement followed by diminishing returns, with a sharper transition under greater initialization mismatch. Under polynomial spectral decay with exponent $\alpha>1$ and leverage compatibility, we establish a squared $L_2$ approximation rate $\mathcal{O}((\kappa_P\log(m/\delta)/m)^\alpha)$ for two-layer networks of width $m$ and trainable proportion $P$, where $\kappa_P=(P/\kappa_1^*+(1-P)/\kappa_0^*)^{-1}$. tldr: 本文为部分可训练的两层神经网络建立了统一的平方 L₂ 逼近误差界 O((κ_P log(m/δ)/m)^α)，揭示了从随机特征到全可训练网络之间存在相变现象：初始改善快速平滑随后收益递减，且初始化失配越大转变越剧烈。
en_tdlr: This paper establishes a uniform squared L₂ approximation rate O((κ_P log(m/δ)/m)^α) for partially trainable two-layer networks, revealing a phase transition from random features to fully trainable networks: rapid smooth initial improvement followed by diminishing returns, with sharper transitions under greater initialization mismatch.
